thought_title: Gather often and Satan's powers fall

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Σπουδάζετε οὖν πυκνότερον συνέρχεσθαι εἰς εὐχαριστίαν θεοῦ καὶ εἰς δόξαν. ὅταν γὰρ πυκνῶς ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γίνεσθε, καθαιροῦνται αἱ δυνάμεις τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ λύεται ὁ ὄλεθρος αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως. [2] οὐδέν ἐστιν ἄμεινον εἰρήνης, ἐν ᾗ πᾶς πόλεμος καταργεῖται ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων.
pass_a_gloss: Be eager, then, to come together more often for thanksgiving to God and for glory. For when you gather together frequently, the powers of Satan are pulled down, and his destruction is undone by the concord of your faith. Nothing is better than peace, in which every war of beings in heaven and beings on earth is brought to nothing.
pass_b_english: So make every effort to meet more often to give thanks to God and to give him glory. When you gather often, Satan's powers are torn down, and the ruin he works comes apart in the oneness of your faith.
Nothing is better than peace. In peace every war of heavenly beings and earthly beings is abolished.

choices.why: εὐχαριστία is both thanksgiving and the Eucharist; Ignatius likely means the eucharistic gathering. 'Give thanks' keeps both senses without forcing one.

choices.english: the ruin he works comes apart
choices.why: λύω is to loosen or dissolve; Satan's destructive work is undone.
rejected: the destruction at which he aims is prevented (ANF; adds 'aims')

choices.english: every war of heavenly beings and earthly beings
choices.why: The genitives name the warring parties, heavenly and earthly beings.
rejected: war of heavenly and earthly things (stiff)

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned. ANF 'show forth His praise' for εἰς δόξαν and 'more precious' for ἄμεινον are loose but not wrong.

notes: Whole chapter 13 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
Possible echo of Colossians 1:20 (peace for things on earth and in heaven); wording not close enough to cite inline.

review.notes: p1 is Ignatius Ephesians 13. Σπουδάζετε οὖν πυκνότερον συνέρχεσθαι εἰς εὐχαριστίαν θεοῦ καὶ εἰς δόξαν matches A 'Be eager, then, to come together more often for thanksgiving to God and for glory' and B 'So make every effort to meet more often to give thanks to God and to give him glory'. ὅταν γὰρ πυκνῶς ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γίνεσθε, καθαιροῦνται αἱ δυνάμεις τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ λύεται ὁ ὄλεθρος αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως is kept in A as 'For when you gather together frequently, the powers of Satan are pulled down, and his destruction is undone by the concord of your faith' and in B as 'When you gather often, Satan's powers are torn down, and the ruin he works comes apart in the oneness of your faith' (αὐτοῦ unpacked as ruin he works; passives and your faith kept). οὐδέν ἐστιν ἄμεινον εἰρήνης, ἐν ᾗ πᾶς πόλεμος καταργεῖται ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων matches A 'Nothing is better than peace, in which every war of beings in heaven and beings on earth is brought to nothing' and B 'Nothing is better than peace. In peace every war of heavenly beings and earthly beings is abolished'. No quoted scripture is cited; the loose Colossians echo is disclosed and not forced. Title names the thought.
